name: Cross-lingual source-silo tilt on non-Anglophone and geopolitics markets
one_line: Forecast each non-Anglophone war market twice with one model (English-wire vs local-language sources) and tilt the price by the difference; unproven: the price over-predicts Russian gains by 5-9 points on 334 resolved territorial markets, but comparable geopolitics rungs are over-priced about as much, the gap is shrinking and fills do not confirm it.
maturity: Experimental; anchor paper scores LLM beliefs against the price path, not outcomes or PnL; no trader found
requires_ai: yes; one LLM reads each language silo and forecasts
edge: Hypothetical: English-source framing bias priced in; comparable measured bias is generic Yes over-pricing
capital: $1k-$10k after validation; ~$200-260 within 5c per market caps size
build_time: 3-5 weeks on top of file 21 (per-theatre archives, leak-free replay)
opportunity_size: Territorial war markets: 108 open, $0.63M liquidity, $135k/day; elections elsewhere pay politics fee
expected_results: no public data, theoretical only; guess 0-0.003 Brier over price, PnL negative after LLM costs
competition: no silo-tilt trader; OSINT specialists, NO-side sellers, arbiter watchers, insiders
flag: grey; war-market ethics, sanctions screening, arbiter tampering and insider exposure
validate: Leak-free replay, 300-650 markets pooled across theatres; kill if tilt = zero or no better than generic Yes shrink
top_risk: Measured bias is generic and shrinking; one theatre cannot give statistical power
solo_fit_reason: Cheap to prototype on file 21's stack and the paper's free MIT dataset, and fee-free war markets suit small maker orders; but where a price-matched control exists the price's pro-capture error is no larger than the generic Yes over-pricing file 24 sells without a model, it is shrinking (+9.0 points in 2025, +5.0 in 2026), fills do not confirm it, and Ukraine alone yields ~50-90 events a year against ~300-650 questions needed at 30 days (more at 7 days).
speed_class: speed-insensitive: daily or weekly silo forecasts; fast arbiter leg belongs to file 13
min_capital: $0 until Phase 1 passes; then ~$3-5k (fixed archive costs)
capacity_ceiling: ~$10-20k: ~150 mid-priced war markets at $50-260 a side
services: Polymarket Data API v1 trades / v2 resolutions
local sources (General Staff, Militarnyi, Defense Express, Telegram via MTProto)
changes_made: Written 2026-09-29 as a speculative-band file on the file 50 / 51 pattern, with the verifiers' lessons applied from the start: deadlines parsed from the question text (Gamma endDate differs by > 2 days on 62 of 334), markets counted at t only if listed and still open, leave-future-out base rate, event-clustered CIs, Yes counts per horizon, fill-based check, paired-difference power, kill criterion as the null.

Anchor paper read in full (arXiv 2607.20441): the models predict the market PRICE 6 h-7 d ahead; 'wrong 64-72%' is scored against the later price path; the paper itself reports Polymarket over-estimating Russian capture by +3.5 pp against outcomes (point-level, 3 of 65 territorial Yes); Ukrainian sources reduce bias but the MAE gain is not significant at market level (p = 0.10-0.37); dataset on Hugging Face (MIT, 54 downloads).

Own no-AI baseline on 334 resolved Russia-Ukraine territorial markets (130 events, $65.8M, 114 Yes): market Brier 0.198 / 0.159 / 0.047 / 0.0053 at listing + 1 d / 30 / 7 / 1 days; midpoint over-predicts Russian gains by +6.7 / +9.4 / +5.4 / +1.4 pp (intervals exclude zero); by year +21.3 (2024) / +9.0 (2025) / +5.0 (2026, interval includes zero).

Control against file 50's other geopolitics by-date rungs: +6.6 / +7.8 / +2.7 / -0.6 pp; the Ukraine-specific excess is +0.1 to +2.7 pp with every interval straddling zero, so the measured bias is the generic over-pricing of dramatic Yes outcomes (file 24), not a demonstrated source-ecosystem effect.

Executed fills (Data API v1 /trades, takerOnly=false, 58 events, 61,953 fills, 3-14 days out): signed error +0.9 pp [-5.2, +6.9] per market, +2.1 share-weighted; same markets at the 7-day midpoint +2.0 [-6.3, +10.1]: underpowered, neither confirms nor refutes. Constant no-AI logit shrink fitted on the first half of events hurt out of sample at 30 days (+0.012 Brier) and helped by 0.003 (n.s.) at 7 days.

Arbiter case located: 'Will Russia capture Myrnohrad by November 15?' ($207,630) went from 0.35c to 96c between 00:14 and 00:39 UTC on 16 November 2025 on the unauthorised ISW edit and resolved Yes with three later rungs; ISW's statement puts the edit on the night of 15-16 November EST, consistent with the tape and not with 404 Media's '10:48 UTC' (file 31 had found no matching market). Meduza shows DeepState objected to Polyglobe, a third-party tool, not to Polymarket itself.

Live capacity by region measured (2,171 geopolitics and elections events; 72 order books): only war markets are fee-free; non-Anglophone elections carry politics_fees (1,883 of 1,916 in Latin America, 1,103 of 1,113 in non-English Europe); open territorial markets hold $0.63M liquidity and $135k a day; Russia-Ukraine mid-band books median 2c spread, ~$200-260 within 5c per side. The brief's Russian parliamentary election closed on 2026-09-20 at $52.1M.

Cite-check + skeptic pass 2026-09-29 (27 sources checked: 25 numbered re-fetched or re-queried incl. the anchor paper's full text, Hindcast full text, Responsible Statecraft and 404 Media archives via curl, Meduza, Wikipedia, GitHub / HN APIs, Gamma and CLOB for the Myrnohrad rung and the Russian election; E7 / E9 passages; 24 confirmed, 3 corrected, 0 removed, 0 unreachable; all writer analyses re-run and reproduced exactly): (1) control comparison qualified: below 35c, where both samples have rungs, Ukraine +4.6 [+1.4, +7.4] vs control +3.3 [-1.1, +6.8]; the 22% of Ukraine rung-horizons at 35c+ carry the largest errors (+14 to +23 points) against 8 control rungs, so a Ukraine-specific component there is untested, not refuted; file 50's own Russia-Ukraine rungs show no over-pricing; town clustering reproduces the event intervals, forecast-month clustering widens the listing interval to include zero. (2) Power re-derived at realistic tilts: the 1,930 figure used a 1.1-logit tilt that failed out of sample; a 0.2-0.3-logit shift (paired SD 0.031-0.046) needs ~180-210 questions for its 0.006-0.009 hindsight gain and ~300-650 for a 0.005 increment at 30 days; at 7 days the best constant shift gains at most 0.003 (hindsight) and needs ~700-1,600; Phase 1 target raised to 300-650 markets pooled across theatres. (3) Fill test: takerOnly=false returns both legs (shares double exactly; share-weighted price equals taker-only on 5 re-pulled markets), so the headline is now the share-weighted +2.1 [-3.9, +7.3]; 61,953 rows = ~4.0M shares matched; fill window includes post-event fills of early-Yes rungs; 35c+ fills -9.0 (12 markets); the '30-day midpoint vs fills' contrast was a horizon mismatch. Also: HF dataset holds five models' ~660k predictions (not four); E7's 'no open-weight model beats the price at t0' is not a Brier comparison in Hindcast (marked unverified); Myrnohrad path re-queried (0.9c at 00:13 UTC, 75c at 00:26, a one-minute 96c print, before the 11:59 PM ET deadline); Wikipedia's '14 November' and 'DeepState accused Polymarket' flagged against ISW / Meduza; /v2/resolutions on two-proposal rungs shows new_version_q and an undocumented reproposed_price. Words: 15 fields 2,411 -> 2,506, three sections 963 -> 950.
open_doubts: The control (file 50's geopolitics rungs) has only 8 rungs priced 35c or above, where the Ukraine error is largest (+14 to +23 points); a source-specific component in mid- and high-priced capture rungs is untested, not refuted.

The fill check (58 events, share-weighted +2.1 points) is too small to confirm or refute the 5-9 point midpoint bias; its window mixes pre- and post-event fills on early-Yes rungs; historical book depth at each horizon is unknown.
Power depends on how large and how market-specific a real silo tilt is; the constant-shift figures (~300-650 questions at 30 days, ~700-1,600 at 7 days) bound a generic correction, not an LLM signal.
Whether Ukrainian- and Russian-reading traders already dominate these books, and how much insider flow they carry, is unmeasured.
The regional capacity classification is a keyword match on event titles and tags; token costs for Ukrainian and Russian text and all per-forecast costs are estimates, not measured runs.

The Ukrainian-gain signal (11 markets, 6 events, priced 37% vs 64% realised) is too thin to interpret; the meaning of the two-proposal `new_version_q` / `reproposed_price` records in /v2/resolutions is undocumented.
